paper.title: [Resistance Mechanisms and Recent Advances in the Third-generation EGFR-TKI Osimertinib for Non-small Cell Lung Cancer].
paper.abstract: Lung cancer is one of the malignant tumors with the highest morbidity and mortality worldwide, and non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) accounts for approximately 85% of all lung cancer cases, with lung adenocarcinoma being the predominant histological subtype. Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) sensitizing mutations are among the most common and important actionable driver alterations in Chinese patients with lung adenocarcinoma, and the advent of EGFR-tyrosine kinase inhibitors (EGFR-TKIs) has inaugurated a new era of precision targeted therapy for lung adenocarcinoma. Osimertinib, a third-generation EGFR-TKI, has become the standard first-line treatment for advanced EGFR-mutated NSCLC and substantially improves survival; however, acquired resistance remains the central limitation to long-term benefit. This review first delineates the distinction between primary and acquired resistance, then summarizes the principal mechanisms underlying acquired resistance to Osimertinib, including EGFR-dependent alterations, bypass pathway activation, histological transformation and cellular plasticity, tumour microenvironment remodelling and metabolic reprogramming, as well as recently identified mechanisms such as SWI/SNF-related, matrix-associated, actin-dependent regulator of chromatin, subfamily A, member 4 (SMARCA4) loss, the YAP1/AXL axis and nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2) epigenetic adaptation. Based on the frequent co-occurrence of multiple resistance mechanisms, we further summarize clinical-scenario-based therapeutic strategies and representative domestic and international studies after resistance to third-generation EGFR-TKIs, so as to provide theoretical references for overcoming Osimertinib resistance. Overall, precise resistance profiling via rebiopsy and liquid biopsy, rational pathway-directed combination therapy, and the integration of next-generation EGFR inhibitors, antibody-drug conjugates and patient-derived organoid drug sensitivity testing are expected to transform EGFR-mutated NSCLC from inevitable resistance into a manageable chronic disease. .

summary.text: This review distinguishes between primary and acquired resistance to Osimertinib in the first-line treatment of advanced EGFR-mutated NSCLC. It summarizes key resistance mechanisms, including EGFR-dependent alterations, bypass pathway activation, histological transformation, and recently identified factors such as SMARCA4 loss, the YAP1/AXL axis, and NRF2 epigenetic adaptation.
